Subject: Post-signature MAP: Staged enablement stitchplan + fallback matrix for Meridian Labs

Hi Alex / Priya —

Congrats again on the signature. Attached is a first-cut "stitchplan" that embeds the MAP into a practical post-signature implementation schedule: rollout phases, canary windows, migration steps, training pods, and a compact fallback matrix for each milestone. My goals with this layout are:

- Keep the go-live risk low by limiting blast radius in Phase A and enabling rapid rollback policies.
- Provide deterministic acceptance gates so your SREs and product owners can sign off after each canary window.
- Make training lightweight and repeatable — small pods that shadow production traffic before full release.

Key highlights (see attachment MAP_StitchPlan_v1.xlsx and Canary_Checklist.pdf):
1) Phase A (Week 1): Embedding + smoke canary (2% traffic, 48h window). Acceptance gates: 95th percentile latency within baseline + no regressions on 12 tracked prompts.
2) Phase B (Weeks 2–3): Staggered migration of additional endpoints, 10% → 30% traffic increments with daily health checks and automated fallback to the hosted shim.
3) Training Cadence: Two 90-minute training pods — one for developers (live prompt debugging + rollback drills) and one for ops (tracing, dashboards, alerting).
4) Fallback matrix: Per-endpoint fallback path (model variant downgrade, regional failover, temporary rate-limit-based soft-fail) and owner for each action.

Action items for this week:
- Alex: confirm two candidate dates for the developer training pods (suggested: Mon 6/22 or Wed 6/24).
- Priya: confirm the list of endpoints for the Phase A smoke canary; we currently have 6 candidates flagged in the sheet.
- Marissa / Karthik / Monica (internal): review the attached canary checklist and call out any controls you want added before Phase B.

I kept the first version compact so we can iterate quickly. If this looks good, we’ll lock in the mutual action dependencies in HubSpot and send a calendar pack.

Thanks —

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
